questions.question: Which State government launched a cryogenic facility to preserve endangered plant species in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tamil Nadu government launched a cryogenic facility in February 2025 to preserve endangered plant species.
 
• This initiative aims to ensure the long-term conservation of the state’s rich biodiversity, especially rare and threatened plants.
 
• Cryogenic preservation involves storing seeds, pollen, and plant tissues at ultra-low temperatures (below -150°C) to maintain their viability for decades or even centuries.
 
• The facility is part of Tamil Nadu’s efforts to combat biodiversity loss due to climate change, habitat destruction, and other anthropogenic factors.
 
• It aligns with global conservation strategies under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and supports national biodiversity goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kerala**

 
 
• Kerala is known for its rich biodiversity and conservation efforts through initiatives like the Silent Valley National Park and the Periyar Tiger Reserve.
 
• The state focuses on sustainable development and eco-tourism to protect its natural resources.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**
 
 
• Karnataka is home to diverse ecosystems, including the Western Ghats, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The state has several conservation programs, such as protecting its unique flora and fauna in Bandipur and Nagarhole National Parks.
 
 
 
• **Telangana**
 
 
• Telangana has undertaken various green initiatives, such as the Haritha Haram program, to increase forest cover and preserve biodiversity.
 
• While the state has focused on afforestation and biodiversity conservation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cryogenic Preservation**

 
 
• Cryogenic preservation is a cutting-edge technology used to maintain the genetic material of species for long-term conservation.
 
• It helps protect species that are at risk of extinction due to habitat loss, climate change, or other challenges.
 
• This technology is widely used in seed banks, botanical research, and biodiversity conservation programs worldwide.

questions.question: Under Article 254(2) of the Indian Constitution, a State law repugnant to a Central law can prevail in the State only if:

options.text: it is passed by a special majority in the State Legislature
It is published in the State Gazette after legislative approval
it is reserved for the President’s consideration and gets his assent
it is certified by the Governor as necessary for public welfare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it is reserved for the President's consideration and gets his assent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 254(2)** of the Indian Constitution provides that if a State law is inconsistent with or repugnant to a Central law, the State law can still prevail in that State, but **only if it is reserved for the President's consideration and receives his assent.**
 
• This provision gives the State Legislature the ability to enact laws on subjects in the Concurrent List, even if they conflict with existing Central laws, provided the President approves.
 
• The President's assent effectively overrides the repugnancy between the State law and the Central law, making the State law operative within the State.
 
• However, Parliament retains the authority to override the State law by passing a new law on the same matter or amending the existing Central law.
 
• This provision ensures a balance of power between the Union and State legislatures while maintaining the supremacy of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 254 of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• Article 254 addresses the inconsistencies between laws made by Parliament and State Legislatures on matters in the Concurrent List.
 
• Article 254(1) specifies that in case of a conflict between a Central and State law, the Central law shall prevail.
 
• Article 254(2) provides an exception, allowing a State law to prevail within the State if it receives the President's assent, despite its inconsistency with a Central law.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India empowers the President to declare Scheduled Areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 244**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 244** of the Constitution of India empowers the President to declare certain areas as Scheduled Areas.
 
• Scheduled Areas are governed under the provisions of the Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These areas have a significant tribal population and are identified to ensure their socio-economic development and protection.
 
• The President, after consulting the Governor of the concerned state, declares the Scheduled Areas.
 
• The Fifth Schedule provides special provisions for administration and governance in these areas, including laws protecting tribal communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 370:**

 
 
• This article granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir, allowing the state to have its own Constitution and autonomy over internal matters, except defense, foreign affairs, and communications.
 
• It was abrogated on August 5, 2019, following the decision by the Indian Parliament.
 
• Post abrogation, Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory, and Ladakh was separated as another Union Territory.
 
 
 
• **Article 338:**
 
 
• Article 338 provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC).
 
• The Commission is tasked with safeguarding the rights of Scheduled Castes and reviewing their socio-economic status.
 
• The NCSC submits annual reports to the President and recommends measures for the betterment of Scheduled Castes.
 
 
 
• **Article 146:**
 
 
• Article 146 deals with the conditions of service of the staff of the Supreme Court.
 
• It empowers the Chief Justice of India to appoint officers and servants of the Supreme Court, subject to certain rules approved by the President.

questions.question: Who among the following scientists is credited with the development of the modern Periodic Law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dmitri Mendeleev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**, a Russian chemist, is credited with the development of the modern Periodic Law and the creation of the first Periodic Table in 1869.
 
• He organized elements based on their atomic masses and grouped them according to their chemical properties, predicting the existence and properties of yet-to-be-discovered elements.
 
• Mendeleev's Periodic Table allowed for the systematic arrangement of elements, enabling scientists to study their relationships and behaviors in a structured manner.
 
• His table was instrumental in the discovery of elements such as gallium, scandium, and germanium, which matched his predictions in terms of properties and atomic masses.
 
• The modern Periodic Table has since been refined to arrange elements by increasing atomic number instead of atomic mass, but Mendeleev's foundational work remains a cornerstone in chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ernest Rutherford**

 
 
• Ernest Rutherford, known as the "Father of Nuclear Physics," discovered the nucleus of the atom in 1911 through his gold foil experiment.
 
• He proposed the planetary model of the atom, where electrons orbit a dense, positively charged nucleus.
 
• Rutherford's work laid the foundation for the understanding of atomic structure but is unrelated to the development of the Periodic Table.
 
 
 
• **John Dalton**
 
 
• John Dalton is known for his Atomic Theory, proposed in 1803, which stated that matter is made up of indivisible particles called atoms.
 
• He also introduced the concept of atomic weight and formulated the Law of Multiple Proportions.
 
• While Dalton's work was a significant step in understanding atomic structure, it preceded the development of the Periodic Table.
 
 
 
• **J.J. Thomson**
 
 
• J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through his cathode ray tube experiment.
 
• He proposed the "Plum Pudding Model" of the atom, where electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere.
 
• Thomson's contributions were pivotal in understanding subatomic particles but were unrelated to the creation of the Periodic Table.

questions.question: Which of the following places is most likely to experience an equable climate with minimal seasonal variation due to its proximity to the sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mumbai**, being a coastal city located along the Arabian Sea, experiences a maritime climate, which is characterized by minimal seasonal temperature variation.
 
• Its close proximity to the sea ensures that the city benefits from the moderating effects of the ocean, leading to an equable climate.
 
• The temperature in Mumbai generally ranges from 25°C to 35°C throughout the year, with no extreme winters or summers.
 
• The high humidity levels in the region, due to its coastal location, further contribute to the steady and mild climate.
 
• Unlike inland cities, Mumbai's climate is less impacted by continental influences, providing it with relatively stable and consistent weather conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amritsar:**

 
 
• Amritsar is an inland city located in Punjab, far from any large water body, and thus experiences a continental climate.
 
• The city witnesses extreme seasonal variations, with very cold winters (temperatures dropping to 4°C) and hot summers (temperatures exceeding 40°C).
 
 
 
• **Bhopal:**
 
 
• Bhopal, located in central India, has a subtropical climate with moderate seasonal variations.
 
• While it does not experience the extreme weather of northern cities, it still lacks the moderating influence of the sea, leading to noticeable temperature fluctuations across seasons.
 
• Summers can be quite hot, with temperatures reaching up to 40°C, while winters are mild with temperatures dropping to around 10°C.
 
 
 
• **Delhi:**
 
 
• Delhi, the capital city of India, is located far from the sea and experiences a typical continental climate.
 
• It is known for its extreme temperature variations, with scorching summers (temperatures exceeding 45°C) and chilly winters (temperatures dropping below 5°C).

questions.question: Which tunnel was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Jammu and Kashmir on 13 January 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Sonamarg tunnel (also known as the Z-Morh tunnel) was inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi on 13 January 2025 in Jammu and Kashmir. 
 
• It is a 6.5 km long road tunnel connecting Gagangir and Sonamarg on the Srinagar-Leh National Highway. 
 
• The tunnel provides year-round all-weather connectivity to Sonamarg and improves access toward Ladakh, enhancing tourism, defence logistics, and local economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
• **Banihal Qazigund tunnel**

 
 
• Part of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project on the Jammu-Kashmir route connecting Banihal to Qazigund. 
 
• Important for rail connectivity through Pir Panjal range
 
 
 
• **Chenani-Nashri Tunnel**
 
 
• Inaugurated in 2017, the Chenani-Nashri tunnel, renamed as the Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee tunnel, is the longest road tunnel in India (9.28 kilometers).
 
• This tunnel connects Udhampur and Ramban districts in Jammu and Kashmir, bypassing the treacherous Patnitop route.
 
• It is a bi-directional tunnel equipped with features such as Integrated Tunnel Control Rooms, video surveillance, and advanced ventilation systems.
 
 
 
• **Nandni Tunnel**
 
 
• The Nandni tunnel is part of the Jammu-Udhampur highway project, which aims to improve road connectivity in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It is a shorter tunnel compared to the Banihal Qazigund and Chenani-Nashri tunnels but plays a critical role in reducing travel time and avoiding landslide-prone areas.

questions.question: Gender disparities significantly affect human development outcomes. Which of the following indicators is NOT part of the Gender Inequality Index (GII)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Food consumption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gender Inequality Index (GII) measures gender disparities across three key dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment, and labor market participation.
 
• **Food consumption** is not included in the GII as it focuses on broader social and economic disparities rather than individual dietary or nutritional patterns.
 
• The reproductive health dimension includes indicators such as maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rates.
 
• The empowerment dimension is assessed through political representation (proportion of parliamentary seats held by women) and educational attainment (secondary education levels among men and women).
 
• The labor market dimension accounts for labor force participation rates among women and men, reflecting economic activity and opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maternal Mortality:**

 
 
• Maternal mortality ratio refers to the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.
 
• It is a critical indicator of reproductive health and reflects access to healthcare and medical services for women during pregnancy and childbirth.
 
• High maternal mortality rates often signify inadequate healthcare infrastructure and gender disparities in access to medical services.
 
 
 
• **Political Representation:**
 
 
• Political representation measures the proportion of parliamentary seats held by women.
 
• This indicator highlights gender equality in decision-making and governance.
 
• Countries with higher political representation of women are often linked to better gender-sensitive policies and improved human development outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Labor Force Participation:**
 
 
• Labor force participation refers to the percentage of working-age individuals actively engaged in the workforce, either employed or seeking employment.
 
• The GII compares labor force participation rates for men and women to evaluate economic disparities.
 
• Lower female participation rates often point to social and structural barriers such as discrimination, lack of childcare support, or societal norms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII):**

 
 
• The GII is a composite measure introduced by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in the Human Development Report.
 
• It highlights disparities in gender-based outcomes across different countries.
 
• By focusing on reproductive health, empowerment, and labor force participation, it provides a comprehensive view of gender inequality globally.

questions.question: The Priest-King statue from Mohenjo-daro, a famous stone sculpture, is predominantly made of which of the following substances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steatite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Priest-King statue from Mohenjo-daro is a famous artifact associated with the **Indus Valley Civilization**, which existed around 2500–1900 BCE.
 
• The statue is predominantly made of **steatite**, a soft stone that is easy to carve and was widely used by the artisans of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Steatite, also known as soapstone, was often treated through a process of heating, which gave it durability and a glazed appearance.
 
• The Priest-King statue is about 17.5 cm high and depicts a male figure adorned with a patterned robe and a prominent headdress, indicating its possible ceremonial or elite significance.
 
• This sculpture reflects the high level of craftsmanship and artistic skills of the Indus Valley artisans, showcasing intricate detailing and a sense of symmetry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terracotta**

 
 
• Terracotta is a type of earthenware made from clay that is fired to a reddish-brown color.
 
• It was extensively used by the Indus Valley Civilization for making figurines, toys, and pottery.
 
• Unlike steatite, terracotta artifacts are unglazed and have a more porous texture.
 
• Examples include small figurines of animals, carts, and human forms, showcasing everyday life and rituals of the civilization.
 
 
 
• **Bronze**
 
 
• Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin and was used by the Indus Valley Civilization to create tools, weapons, and sculptures.
 
• A famous example is the "Dancing Girl" statue, which is made of bronze and demonstrates the lost-wax casting technique.
 
• Unlike the Priest-King, which is made of steatite, bronze artifacts reflect the civilization's advanced knowledge of metallurgy.
 
 
 
• **Limestone**
 
 
• Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed largely of calcium carbonate, used in various ancient civilizations for construction and sculptures.
 
• However, there is no evidence of the Indus Valley Civilization using limestone for artifacts like the Priest-King statue.
 
• Limestone was more commonly associated with other ancient civilizations, such as the Egyptians, for building pyramids and statues.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges belongs to the Peninsular Plateau?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajanta range**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ajanta range is part of the Peninsular Plateau, specifically located in the western part of Maharashtra.
 
• This range is known for its undulating terrain and forms part of the Deccan Plateau, which is one of the oldest landmasses in India.
 
• The Ajanta range is also home to the famous Ajanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that dates back to the 2nd century BCE.
 
• Geologically, the range is composed of volcanic rocks, primarily basalt, which is characteristic of the Deccan Traps.
 
• The Ajanta range plays a crucial role in influencing the local climate and acts as a watershed for several rivers in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shivalik range:**

 
 
• The Shivalik range, also known as the Outer Himalayas, is the southernmost mountain range of the Himalayan system.
 
• It stretches from Jammu and Kashmir in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, covering parts of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and other states.
 
• This range is geologically young and is composed of unconsolidated sediments such as sand, gravel, and silt.
 
• It is not part of the Peninsular Plateau but instead belongs to the Himalayan mountain system.
 
 
 
• **Zanskar range:**
 
 
• The Zanskar range is a part of the Trans-Himalayan region and lies in the northern state of Ladakh.
 
• It is a high-altitude range with peaks exceeding 6,000 meters and is characterized by extreme climatic conditions.
 
• The Zanskar range is home to many glaciers and serves as a source for rivers like the Zanskar River.
 
• This range does not belong to the Peninsular Plateau as it is part of the Himalayan system.
 
 
 
• **Karakoram range:**
 
 
• The Karakoram range is one of the major mountain ranges in the northern region of the Indian subcontinent, extending across India, Pakistan, and China.
 
• It is known for housing some of the world’s highest peaks, including K2, the second-highest mountain in the world.
 
• The range is characterized by glaciers such as the Siachen Glacier and Baltoro Glacier.
 
• As part of the Himalayan mountain system, the Karakoram range is not associated with the Peninsular Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau:**
 
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is one of the oldest and most stable landmasses in India, covering large parts of southern and central India.
 
• It is divided into two main sections: the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The plateau is characterized by flat-topped hills, valleys, and volcanic rock formations like the Deccan Traps.
 
• Major mountain ranges of the Peninsular Plateau include the Aravalli Hills, Satpura range, Vindhya range, and Ajanta range.

questions.question: As announced on 30 April 2025, what major decision did the Indian Cabinet take regarding the upcoming decennial census?

options.text: To conduct the first ever digital-only census
To include a caste-based enumeration in the next census

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To include a caste-based enumeration in the next census​.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On** 30 April 2025**, the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs (**CCPA**) decided to include caste enumeration in the upcoming decennial census exercise. 
 
• This will be the first time in decades that comprehensive caste data beyond SC/ST categories is collected nationwide during the census. 
 
• Caste data will be captured electronically during the census process, helping inform policy on reservation, socio-economic planning, and representation. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To postpone the census indefinitely**

 
 
• Postponing the census indefinitely would disrupt crucial data collection, which forms the basis for policy formulation, resource allocation, and governance in India.
 
• The census is conducted every 10 years, and postponement would hinder the availability of updated demographic data needed for development planning.
 
 
 
• **To conduct the first ever digital-only census**
 
 
• The 2027 Census is set to be digitally oriented with mobile apps and self-enumeration options, but the key announced cabinet decision on 30 April focused on caste inclusion. 
 
• A digital component improves data quality and timeliness in census operations.
 
 
 
• **To eliminate caste data collection**
 
 
• Eliminating caste data collection from the census would affect the understanding of India's socio-economic structure and hinder targeted policy-making for marginalized communities.
 
• Caste data plays a critical role in designing affirmative action programs and understanding the needs of various social groups.

questions.question: Which of the following energy sources remained the dominant contributor to India’s renewable energy growth, accounting for 47% of the total installed renewable energy capacity in 2024?

questions.question: What is self-induction?

options.text: Induction of EMF in one coil due to a current in a nearby coil
Induction of EMF in a coil due to motion in a magnetic field
Induction of EMF in a coil due to a change in its own current
Generation of current in a coil due to temperature changes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Induction of EMF in a coil due to a change in its own current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Self-induction** is the phenomenon in which an electromotive force (EMF) is induced in a coil due to a change in the current flowing through the same coil.
 
• The induced EMF opposes the change in current, as per **Lenz's Law**, and is mathematically expressed as **E = -L (dI/dt)**, where L is the self-inductance of the coil.
 
• Self-inductance is a property of a coil that depends on its dimensions, number of turns, and the medium surrounding it. It is measured in **henry (H)**.
 
• Self-induction plays a critical role in devices like **transformers, inductors, and electrical circuits** where controlling or opposing rapid changes in current is essential.
 
• It is an important principle in electromagnetic theory and is widely applied in technologies like AC systems and communication devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**

 
 
• Electromagnetic induction is the process of inducing an EMF or current in a conductor due to the relative motion between the conductor and a magnetic field or due to changes in the magnetic flux.
 
• The concept of self-induction is a specific case of electromagnetic induction where the coil induces EMF in itself rather than in another coil.
 
• These principles are fundamental to modern electrical engineering and power systems.

questions.question: Which method is employed in the refining of petroleum to separate crude oil from high boiling point fractions like lubricating oils?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fractional Distillation**__.

__
 
• **Fractional distillation** is the primary method employed for refining crude oil and separating its components based on their boiling points.
 
• During fractional distillation, crude oil is heated to a high temperature, causing it to vaporize.
 
• The vaporized crude oil is passed into a fractionating column, where it cools and condenses at different levels based on the boiling points of its components.
 
• Lower boiling point fractions like gasoline and kerosene condense at the top of the column, while higher boiling point fractions like lubricating oils and bitumen condense at the bottom.
 
• This process ensures the separation of crude oil into various useful products, including gasoline, diesel, kerosene, lubricating oils, waxes, and asphalt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vacuum filtration**

 
 
• Vacuum filtration is a method used to separate solids from liquids using a vacuum pump to create suction.
 
• It is commonly employed in laboratories for purifying solutions or isolating precipitates.
 
• It is designed for solid-liquid separation rather than liquid-liquid separation.
 
 
 
• **Differential extraction**
 
 
• Differential extraction is a process used to separate compounds based on their solubility in different solvents.
 
• It is commonly used in pharmaceutical industries and forensic science to isolate and purify specific components from mixtures.
 
 
 
• **Rotary sublimation**
 
 
• Rotary sublimation is a technique used to purify substances that can transition directly from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase.
 
• This method is mostly employed for purifying volatile compounds, such as certain organic substances.

questions.question: If 3 times the mother's age is 29 years more than 5 times her daughter's age, and 2 times the daughter's age is 2 years less than the mother's age, then what is the difference (in years) between the ages of the mother and the daughter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the second condition: **Mother's age (M)** − 2 × **Daughter's age (D)** = 2 ⇒ M = 2D + 2.

Substitute M into the first condition: 3(2D + 2) − 5D = 29.

6D + 6 − 5D = 29 ⇒ D = 23 years.

Then M = 2(23) + 2 = 48 years.

**Age Difference** = 48 − 23 = 25 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the **Mother's age** be M and **Daughter's age** be D.

Equation 1: 3M − 5D = 29

Equation 2: M − 2D = 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec846d94cf8a820e67188e7e39b6079403da74d10f05c5f378ce504e754e1661.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ From Eq 2: M = 2D + 2

⇒ Substitute M in Eq 1: 3(2D + 2) − 5D = 29

⇒ 6D + 6 − 5D = 29

⇒ D = 23 years

⇒ M = 2(23) + 2 = 48 years

⇒ Difference = M − D = 48 − 23 = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains constant regardless of the number of years that pass.

Substitution Method

Express one variable in terms of the other from the simpler equation and substitute it into the second equation to solve for both.</p

N₁ = 3³ × (3²)² × 1 = 3⁷

N₂ = 3² × 13² × 1 = 3² × 13²

N₃ = (3²)³ × 13² × (2 × 3²)² = 3⁶ × 13² × 2² × 3⁴ = 2² × 3¹⁰ × 13²

LCM = Take the **highest power** of each prime factor present: 2², 3¹⁰, and 13².

**∴ The correct answer is 2² × 3¹⁰ × 13².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (A) = 3³ × 9² × 1³

Second number (B) = 3² × 13² × 1⁸

Third number (C) = 9³ × 13² × 18²

**Formula Used:**

LCM of numbers expressed as product of primes = Product of highest powers of all prime factors involved.

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 3³ × (3²)² × 1 = 3³ × 3⁴ = 3⁷

⇒ B = 3² × 13² × 1 = 3² × 13²

⇒ C = (3²)³ × 13² × (2 × 3²)² = 3⁶ × 13² × 2² × 3⁴ = 2² × 3¹⁰ × 13²

⇒ Prime factors involved: 2, 3, and 13.

⇒ Highest power of 2 = 2²

⇒ Highest power of 3 = 3¹⁰

⇒ Highest power of 13 = 13²

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3¹⁰ × 13²

**∴ The correct answer is 2² × 3¹⁰ × 13².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Prime Factors

Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the product of the **lowest powers** of common prime factors.

LCM and HCF Relationship

For two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.

LCM of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).</p

questions.question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(7) part of a tank in 18 hours, and pipe Q can fill (5)/(9) part of the same tank in 25 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 3 hours, then both were closed.  Pipe P 63 315 5

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 82% of the registered voters cast their vote and 4% of the votes polled were found invalid. The winning candidate got 60% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1968 votes. How many voters were registered?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **total registered voters** be X.

**Valid votes** = X × 82% × 96%

Winning margin = 60% − 40% = 20% of **valid votes**.

⇒ X × 0.82 × 0.96 × 0.20 = 1968

⇒ X = 1968 ÷ (0.82 × 0.96 × 0.20) = 12500.

**∴ The correct answer is 12500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f7de1e0359dda4f20d58e91fa74ab8d81004a9a9626c465d81a1332104067ed.png] 

**Given:**

Voters polled = 82% | Invalid votes = 4% | Winner share = 60% of valid | Margin = 1968

⇒ Let **Total Voters** = 100 units

⇒ Polled votes = 82 units

⇒ Valid votes = 82 × (100 − 4)% = 82 × 0.96 = 78.72 units

⇒ Winner gets = 60% of 78.72 | Loser gets = 40% of 78.72

⇒ Difference (Margin) = 20% of 78.72 units

⇒ 0.20 × 78.72 units = 15.744 units

⇒ 15.744 units = 1968

⇒ 1 unit = 1968 ÷ 15.744 = 125

⇒ 100 units = 125 × 100 = 12500

**∴ The correct answer is 12500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election Base Calculations

Always identify the base: **Valid Votes** = (Total × Polled%) − Invalid. The percentage share of candidates is usually calculated on valid votes unless stated otherwise.

Winning Margin Rule

Margin = (Winner% − Loser%) × Valid Votes. If there are only two candidates, Loser% = 100% − Winner%.

Successive Percentage Method

Election problems can be solved as **Successive Multiplication**: Total × Vote% × Valid% × Margin% = Winning Margin Value.</p

questions.question: If sin θ=(p²-1)/(p²+1) and θ is an acute angle, then find the value of cos θ.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **Right-Angled Triangle**, if **sin θ** = (p² − 1)/(p² + 1), then the **Perpendicular (P)** = p² − 1 and **Hypotenuse (H)** = p² + 1.

Using the **standard triplet**: (2p)² + (p² − 1)² = (p² + 1)², the **Base (B)** is 2p.

Therefore, **cos θ** = Base / Hypotenuse = 2p / (p² + 1).

**∴ The correct answer is (2p)/(p²+1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sin θ = (p² − 1) / (p² + 1)

**Formula Used:** cos² θ = 1 − sin² θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5cd2d0d159700e5b9b42595cb1904f6ceda416698ba38b15ce93f184e7dfed88.png] 

⇒ cos² θ = 1 − [(p² − 1) / (p² + 1)]²

⇒ cos² θ = [(p² + 1)² − (p² − 1)²] / (p² + 1)²

⇒ cos² θ = [ (p⁴ + 2p² + 1) − (p⁴ − 2p² + 1) ] / (p² + 1)²

⇒ cos² θ = [ 4p² ] / (p² + 1)²

⇒ cos θ = √[ (2p)² / (p² + 1)² ]

⇒ cos θ = 2p / (p² + 1)

**∴ The correct answer is (2p)/(p²+1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The fundamental identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, from which we derive sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.

Pythagorean Triplets

For any value p, the expressions 2p, p²−1, and p²+1 always form a **Pythagorean triplet** where p²+1 is the **hypotenuse**.</p

questions.question: In covering a distance of 52 km, Anmol takes 6 hours more than Nikhil. If Anmol doubles his speed, then he would take 7 hours less than Nikhil. Anmol's speed is:

When **Anmol** doubles his **speed** (Ratio 1 : 2), his **time** ratio becomes 2 : 1.

The difference in time units = 2 − 1 = 1 unit.

Actual time difference = 6 hours (late) + 7 hours (early) = 13 hours.

Original time taken by **Anmol** = 2 units = 2 × 13 = 26 hours.

**Anmol** speed = Distance ÷ Original Time = 52 ÷ 26 = 2 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/hr.**

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Original time (T₁) = 52 ÷ s

⇒ New time (T₂) = 52 ÷ 2s

⇒ Time difference = T₁ − T₂ = (Nikhil + 6) − (Nikhil − 7) = 13 hours

⇒ (52 ÷ s) − (52 ÷ 2s) = 13

⇒ (104 − 52) ÷ 2s = 13

⇒ 52 ÷ 2s = 13

⇒ 26 ÷ s = 13

⇒ s = 26 ÷ 13 = 2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/hr.**

Speed-Time Relationship

For a constant **distance**, **speed** is inversely proportional to **time** (S ∝ 1/T). If speed is doubled, time is halved.

Time Difference Concept

When one case is **late** and the other is **early**, the total time difference is the sum of both values (x late + y early = x + y difference).

Average Speed Formula

If a person covers equal distances at speeds **u** and **v**, the **Average Speed** = 2uv ÷ (u + v).</p

questions.question: The average weight of Salil, Mukund and Sachin is 45 kg. If the average weight of Salil and Mukund is 44 kg and that of Mukund and Sachin is 48 kg, then the weight of Mukund (in kg) is:

Weight of **Mukund** = (Sum of two pairs) − (Total Sum of three)

Finding Overlapping Values

questions.question: Simplify: x(6x − 9) + 6(x² − 3) + 19

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expand the expression directly by multiplying terms: **x(6x − 9)** gives **6x² − 9x**.

Expand the second part: **6(x² − 3)** gives **6x² − 18**.

Combine all terms: **(6x² − 9x) + (6x² − 18) + 19**.

Group like terms: **(6x² + 6x²) − 9x + (−18 + 19) = 12x² − 9x + 1**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12x² − 9x + 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** x(6x − 9) + 6(x² − 3) + 19

**Formula Used:** Distributive Property a(b + c) = ab + ac

⇒ Step 1: Open the first bracket

⇒ x × 6x − x × 9 = 6x² − 9x

⇒ Step 2: Open the second bracket

⇒ 6 × x² − 6 × 3 = 6x² − 18

⇒ Step 3: Write the full expression together

⇒ 6x² − 9x + 6x² − 18 + 19

⇒ Step 4: Combine the coefficients of **x²** and **constant terms**

⇒ (6 + 6)x² − 9x + (19 − 18)

⇒ 12x² − 9x + 1

**∴ The correct answer is 12x² − 9x + 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always solve terms inside **Brackets** first, then **Orders**, **Division/Multiplication**, and finally **Addition/Subtraction**.

Like Terms

Terms with the same **variable** and **exponent** (like 6x² and 6x²) can be added or subtracted by combining their coefficients.

Distributive Property

Multiplying a sum by a number is the same as multiplying each addend by the number and then adding the products: **a(b + c) = ab + ac**.</p
